sources.title: A Theorem on the Distribution of Weights in a Systematic Code
sources.locator: Publisher abstract; explicit identity verified in Lomonaco2006 handout and independently derived in the research note
sources.relationship: The classical dual weight-enumerator transform supplies the general N40 count after the binary-kernel translation.
sources.comparison_limit: The complete1963proof was not retrieved. This establishes classical attribution of the identity, not that MacWilliams discussed these QC-GHP absorbing sets or gave a low-dimensional M_j-only formula.

sources.title: The MacWilliams and Pless Identities: A Summary
sources.locator: Theorem1 p1 and explicit parity-check/dual enumeration example pp2–3
sources.relationship: Primary instructor exposition verifies the binary weight-enumerator identity used here; its degree-four coefficient is the counting baseline.
sources.comparison_limit: The handout is an exposition, not the original priority source. Our all-2^m-row-messages form permits dependent check rows, justified separately by constant-size fibers.

sources.title: Codes and designs for quantum error correction: some recent developments through combinatorics
sources.locator: Section3 p37/PDF6, Proposition3.8 and following even-four-configuration paragraph; references[9],[16]
sources.relationship: Even configurations correspond to binary dependencies; the even four-triple configuration is Pasch. This is explicit prior terminology and substance for the kernel bridge in complete Steiner designs.
sources.comparison_limit: Our generic cubic linear incidence proof does not need complete-design regularity. The bridge itself is classical elementary linear algebra, not a new mathematical phenomenon. Later open even-freeness questions in this2014survey were not screened for inventory or current status.

sources.title: High-girth Steiner triple systems
sources.locator: Author preprint first3pages,Theorem1.1/Definition1.2; publisher bibliographic milestones
sources.relationship: Resolves the historical Erdos high-girth existence problem cited by Beezer, preventing it from being indexed as currently open.
sources.comparison_limit: Small dense (j,j−2) configurations are different from all Beezer generators. Does not by itself answer Beezer minimum-order fixed-generator-girth problem. Full proof not audited in this block.

sources.title: Binary MacWilliams identity: public Lean source
sources.relationship: General rational-evaluation binary dual weight-enumerator identity, over arbitrary ZMod2 submodules, with x != -1. Related classical background for the full-incidence count.
sources.comparison_limit: Both Lean files inspected; no sorry/admit/custom axiom/native_decide tokens found. Not compiled or axiom-audited here. Declared Lean v4.32.0-rc1 differs from our pinned v4.36.0-rc1. No absorbing-support/Pasch/socket/complex cyclic count bridge in this two-file source tree. No first-formalization claim for our work.
